name: How long does apartment construction take in Los Angeles from permit to completion?

mainEntity.name: How long does a typical apartment construction project take in Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, or Burbank?
mainEntity.text: How long does a typical apartment construction project take in Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, or Burbank?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apartment construction timelines in Los Angeles are usually longer than owners expect because the schedule includes more than field construction. For a small to mid-size project, actual building time can run about 12 to 24 months, but the total timeline from concept to occupancy often stretches much longer once design, permitting, revisions, financing, and inspections are included. Cities such as Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, Burbank, and North Hollywood can have different review rhythms, so the same project may move at different speeds depending on jurisdiction and site conditions. The biggest schedule risks are entitlement issues, utility approvals, structural revisions, and changes requested late in the process. If timing matters, ask the builder for a schedule that separates preconstruction, permit processing, rough framing, MEP work, inspections, and final closeout. A realistic schedule should also include float for unexpected delays, because multifamily projects are especially sensitive to plan-check iterations and long-lead materials.
acceptedAnswer.description: A small apartment project in Los Angeles can take 12 to 24 months for construction alone, and much longer when entitlement, design, and permit review are included. Site complexity, design changes, utility coordination, and city review times often add several months before work begins.
